summary:
AstroCare AI is a software prototype developed to support astronaut health monitoring during space missions.

The system provides separate interfaces for astronauts and medical officers. Astronauts can enter health-related information and view their wellness records. Medical officers can review submitted records, monitor alerts, and access health analytics through a centralized dashboard.

The application includes manual health data entry, simulated health readings, wellness tracking, an AI-assisted information interface, and research data integration. NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) research data and NASA DONKI space-weather information are used to demonstrate how relevant spaceflight research and environmental context can support health-monitoring workflows.

The system is developed using React, TypeScript, Python FastAPI, and SQLite.

AstroCare AI is currently a demonstration prototype. It does not connect to live astronaut wearable devices and is not a certified medical diagnostic system.
details:
AstroCare AI is an astronaut health monitoring and decision-support software platform designed to support crew health management during space missions.

The platform provides two separate interfaces for astronauts and medical officers. Astronauts can record health measurements, monitor vital signs, track wellness, view health trends, and receive alerts. Medical officers can review astronaut health records, monitor crew information, analyze trends, and add clinical review notes.

The system monitors key health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature, and sleep duration. It includes statistical anomaly detection using personal health baselines to highlight unusual changes. The platform also provides mental wellness tracking, a breathing exercise feature, and an AI-assisted health information interface.

AstroCare AI supports NASA research dataset exploration through CSV and Excel uploads. It also incorporates NASA space-weather information to provide additional mission-environment context.

The application is developed using React, TypeScript, Python, FastAPI, and SQLite. Three.js is used to create an interactive 3D aerospace interface. The backend manages authentication, role-based access, health records, and shared information between astronauts and medical officers.

The main benefit is to organize astronaut health information in one platform and make it easier for medical teams to review health trends and wellness records. Its creative approach combines astronaut health monitoring, medical collaboration, research data exploration, and an immersive aerospace user interface.

AstroCare AI is currently a software prototype. It uses manually entered data, simulated telemetry, and research datasets where applicable. It is not a certified medical diagnostic system and does not replace professional medical decisions.
